findings.evidence: "The benefits team tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Name the specific document (e.g., "a printed copy of the budget summary").
findings.violation: "A printed copy" has no antecedent - the prior sentence is about tracking a budget, not a document, so it's unclear what staff can actually request.

findings.evidence: "The stipend clock resumes on their first day back."
findings.fix: Define what the "stipend clock" tracks, or replace the phrase with explicit reference to the 90-day eligibility period.
findings.violation: "Stipend clock" is used without ever being defined, so it's unclear whether it refers to the 90-day service requirement, the benefit-year window, or something else.

findings.evidence: "The workspace must sit inside the employee's primary residence... A workspace located in a shared coworking space does not qualify... A workspace used only occasionally for calls does not meet the bar..."
findings.fix: Reformat the criteria as a bulleted checklist.
findings.violation: Nine short, repetitive "A workspace..." sentences are strung together in prose instead of a structured list, making the actual eligibility criteria hard to locate and verify.

findings.evidence: "Employees must submit the receipt, the manager's approval form, and the original purchase order before the review begins."
findings.fix: Clarify the sequence, e.g., require only a request form up front, with the approval form produced as an output of the manager's review.
findings.violation: This requires the manager's approval form as an input before any review happens, but the Approval Timeline section describes the manager reviewing and approving the request afterward - the approval form can't precede the approval it documents.

findings.evidence: "the original purchase order" (How to Apply) vs. "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests." (Required Documentation)
findings.fix: Reconcile the two sections into one consistent documentation requirement.
findings.location: How to Apply section vs. Required Documentation section
findings.violation: The two sections conflict on what documentation is actually required to submit a claim.

findings.evidence: "The requester gets an automatic reminder after three days."
findings.fix: State explicitly what event starts the three-day countdown and reconcile it with the two-day review commitment.
findings.violation: The countdown's starting point is unspecified, and three days is inconsistent with the two-business-day review window stated in the same section.

findings.evidence: "Additionally, employees shall retain receipts for one year after the purchase date."
findings.fix: Replace with "must keep" to match the document's style.
findings.violation: "Shall retain" breaks from the plain "must/keep" phrasing used elsewhere in the policy, an inconsistent register.

findings.evidence: "The finance office conducts an evaluation of every submitted receipt before it approves the amount." / "unused stipend amounts do not roll over to the next benefit year."
findings.fix: Add the specific stipend amount or cap per equipment category.
findings.violation: A section titled "Reimbursement Amounts" never states any actual dollar figure, percentage, or cap - the core content the heading promises is missing.

findings.evidence: "this office may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Name the specific office responsible for the photo check.
findings.violation: "This office" has no clear antecedent - the document names a benefits team, finance office, people operations office, and finance liaison elsewhere, but not which performs this check.

findings.evidence: "The stipend covers one claim per employee per benefit year." (Eligibility) vs. "the policy applies to one device per category per employee" (Restrictions and Exceptions)
findings.fix: Clarify whether the annual limit is one claim total or one per category.
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions vs. Eligibility section
findings.violation: The benefit-year limit is stated as one claim total in Eligibility but as one device per category (implying multiple claims) in Restrictions and Exceptions, and these limits are never reconciled.

findings.evidence: "the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device because fieldwork regularly takes the employee away from the single fixed desk that the standard equipment list assumes every applicant has for the whole benefit year while the finance office tracks the second device against the same annual amount that the equipment catalog publishes for each category."
findings.fix: Split into separate sentences and resolve whether one or two devices per category are permitted.
findings.violation: This single run-on sentence contradicts itself by stating the policy covers "one device per category" while describing approval for "a second device," and it crams multiple unrelated conditions into one unreadable sentence.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person to match the rest of the document.
findings.violation: This section switches to second-person "you" while the rest of the policy uses third person ("employees," "the applicant"), an inconsistent voice.

findings.fix: Define "stipend item" or replace it with the established term "equipment."
findings.violation: "Stipend item" is used repeatedly but never defined, and it's unclear whether it is synonymous with "equipment" as used elsewhere in the policy.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Merge this section into "How to Apply" or clearly differentiate its purpose from that section.
findings.violation: This duplicates the How to Apply section's purpose but lists a different, inconsistent set of steps (omitting the manager's approval form and purchase order), creating redundancy and ambiguity about the real process.

findings.evidence: "The finance liaison reviews the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Remove this duplicated paragraph or replace it with actual special-case guidance, and resolve the ownership conflict.
findings.violation: This duplicates the Program Overview's opening sentences almost verbatim but attributes budget oversight to a different party ("finance liaison" vs. "benefits team"), and the content has nothing to do with "Special Cases."

findings.evidence: "The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout... Once approved, the team schedules the reimbursement for the next pay cycle."
findings.fix: Consolidate the division of responsibility between the benefits team, manager, and finance office into one authoritative description.
findings.violation: This overlaps with and conflicts with Approval Timeline (manager approves the request) and Reimbursement Amounts (finance office approves the amount), leaving approval authority unclear.

findings.evidence: "The escalation of repeat requests happens automatically within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Define "repeat request" and describe the escalation steps and who they are routed to.
findings.violation: "Repeat requests" and the escalation process are introduced with no definition, leaving it unclear what qualifies as a repeat request or what the escalation entails.

findings.evidence: "The people operations office tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate paragraph and state budget-tracking ownership once, consistently, in a single location.
findings.violation: This duplicates Program Overview content nearly verbatim with a third, different party credited for budget tracking (benefits team, finance liaison, and now people operations office), and "every entry" has no antecedent since the preceding sentence describes a budget, not a catalog of entries.
